thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: P1 - GCP europe-west9 GPU quota exhausted. Autoscaler failing to provision new GPU nodes; inference-api queue growing rapidly. Alerts: gpu_util=100%, scale_attempts failing with QUOTA_EXCEEDED. Link: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/5067894321
oncall-jen: I'm on it. Starting triage — will gather metrics and impact.
infra-mike: seeing quota errors from GCE "Quota has been exhausted for resource 'GPUS' in region europe-west9". Recent stack:
``` 
  2026-03-15T10:12:05Z scale-controller ERROR: provision failed: QUOTA_EXCEEDED (project: redwood-prod, region: europe-west9)
  2026-03-15T10:12:06Z node-manager WARN: pool-gpu-eu-9 at 100% allocation
```
sre-alejandro: queue length on inference-api namespace: 1.2k pending requests; p95 latency degraded to ~4.6s -> many timeouts. Customers seeing 503/504.
eng-runtime-sam: quick note — fallback routing to cpu-only instances is active for some endpoints but it's slower and many requests are timing out before retry. We can: 1) evict non-critical warm pools, 2) reduce batch windows, 3) temporarily route traffic to eu-west1/eu-west4, or 4) fallback to smaller quantized model variant.
oncall-jen: actionable checklist:
- (A) Who can open a GCP support case and request emergency GPU quota bump?
- (B) Who can evict warm pools / reduce priority jobs now?
- (C) CS to assess customer impact and prepare status text.
- (D) Ops to consider cross-region reroute.

infra-mike: I've opened a GCP ticket (support case started, reference: C-xxxxx). ETA from GCP is unknown but typically multi-hour. Meanwhile I'm going to evict low-priority warm pools and kill/scale down benching jobs.
eng-runtime-sam: I'll prepare a quick runtime config flip: toggle model route for the heavy-gen endpoint to `redwood-small-quantized:v2` and reduce `batch_window_ms` from 40 -> 10 to drop memory pressure. Command:
```
# internal admin API (prod) - do not run outside coord
POST https://admin.internal/v1/routes/rollout
Payload: {"route":"/v1/generate","model":"redwood-small-quantized:v2","batch_window_ms":10}
```
prod-support-lina: CS: we have ~30 high-severity customer reports in EU (timeouts during inference). One enterprise customer (acct: ACCT-8432) seeing repeated 504s. We should publish a brief status update.
cs-raj: drafting status page & customer note now, suggested text below — please approve: 
"We are experiencing elevated errors and latency for inference requests in GCP europe-west9. Our engineers are mitigating and routing traffic to alternate regions. We will provide updates every 30 minutes. No data loss reported."

oncall-jen: approved. @prod-support-lina please post and flag enterprise contacts. Also @infra-mike start evictions now, @eng-runtime-sam proceed with route change (canary first).
deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated for route /v1/generate -> redwood-small-quantized:v2 (10% traffic). Canary ID: canary-5067894321.
infra-mike: evicted 12 warm-pool instances (non-critical batch preparers), freed ~48 GPUs. Autoscaler retried and started provisioning 10 nodes — some allocations succeeded (5 nodes), some still hit quota.
sre-alejandro: monitoring: queue dropped from 1200 -> 420 in 8m after canary and evictions; p95 latency down to 2.1s for canary traffic. Error rate overall reduced from 18% -> 6%.
eng-runtime-sam: rolling broader rollout to 40% now (watching OOMs). Also lowered max_tokens to 512 for heavy endpoints to reduce mem usage.
prod-support-lina: status posted to status.redwood.ai and customers emailed. Sample: "We're experiencing service degradation in europe-west9; traffic is being rerouted. We're mitigating now and will update in 30 mins." :thumbsup:
cs-raj: notifying affected enterprise contacts via phone + email.
infra-mike: quick infra note — we found several long-running pre-warm jobs (internal experiments) consuming reserved GPUs in the project. Those have been force-terminated. Also moved a small reserved pool from dedicated-usg to europe-west1 as temporary relief.
oncall-jen: what is current risk? expected remaining impact?
sre-alejandro: risk: medium. If GCP doesn't grant additional quota and traffic returns to normal peak, we could see recurring stalls. Mitigations in place: cross-region fallback, model downgrade, warm-pool eviction. Long-term: request quota increase & automation to fallback more aggressively when quota errors are detected.
oncall-jen: assigning followups:
- Postmortem owner: @eng-runtime-sam
- Quota escalation & cloud case owner: @infra-mike
- Customer comms owner: @prod-support-lina / @cs-raj
- Runbook update: @sre-alejandro

eng-runtime-sam: post-incident quick actions I'll do now: add a pre-check in the scale controller to stop new canaries when GCE QUOTA_EXCEEDED seen, backoff longer, and add an automated cross-region shift (config flag). Also I'll add a temporary runtime flag to reduce batch_window on heavy routes.
infra-mike: update: GCP responded — temporary quota bump to allow +16 GPUs in europe-west9 for 2 hours (they asked us to list projects/nodes). I've accepted. Provisioner is bringing up remaining nodes.
incident-bot: Metrics update: queue length now 78 pending, error_rate 1.8%, p95 latency ~1.9s. Service appears to be recovering. :white_check_mark:
oncall-jen: Great work, thanks all. I'll hand off to @infra-mike for monitoring and closure. I will write the incident summary.
infra-mike: Taking over monitoring for next 2 hours. Filing post-incident ticket and runbook updates.
sre-alejandro: Postmortem notes to capture: root cause (project-level GPU quota reached due to runaway pre-warm jobs + unexpected traffic spike), why autoscaler didn't failover earlier, improvements to fallback automation, customer comms timeline.
prod-support-lina: Customer comms sent, CS team on standby. No escalations open at this moment.
eng-runtime-sam: I'll own the postmortem and follow up with a PR for the runtime flags.
incident-bot: Incident status: RECOVERED -> degraded service cleared. Close P1 to P2 for postmortem follow-up. First alert: 5067894321, resolved: 5067895521.
oncall-jen: closing this thread. If anything regresses ping escalation channel. Thanks everyone. :bow:
